task: apply to a job online (Indeed, Workday, LinkedIn Easy Apply, company career portals): find the posting, start the application, fill the multi-page form, upload or attach a resume, answer the screening questions, submit; complete when the application-submitted confirmation is on screen. Surface pinned: a job board or employer application portal on the web. Variants: resume writing, job-search browsing without submitting, and interview preparation do not belong.

tree.label: Apply for a job online
tree.note: do 1, then 2 - repeat 2.1 and 2.2 until a posting survives the read (skni rejects three on location alone before committing). 3 where the platform puts it: at the very first step (nI4K, and the session ends there), between the posting and the form (WjDI, DzPw, cXKe, CDOH), or only after the availability preferences (15nS, dz2Z) - the Indeed keepers arrive signed in and never see it. 4 before anything else on the profile marketplace (8dGC). then 5 on the employer portals, or 6 in its place on the marketplaces (8dGC, a2Q4). then 7. 8 where the platform demands more after the submit - an assessment (CL48, skni) or an identity check (GPCO). 9 where a confirmation or dashboard exists; on ERA the application stays editable there until the vacancy closes.

children.label: Reach the hiring portal
children.note: 1.1 and 1.2 together on search-engine entries (CDOH, 15nS, cXKe), 1.3 where the employer runs two portals, 1.4 on direct-link entries (WjDI, DzPw). 1.5 where the session starts signed in. 1.6 fires throughout the task, not just at entry - the platform raises them at whatever point it wants.

questions.question: Should you apply classification and location filters, or just search by keyword?

questions.question: What type of employment are you looking for?

questions.check: What job-type options does the filter show?

questions.question: Should you filter the job search results by a specific company?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to prioritize or avoid specific employers based on their personal preferences or career goals.
questions.check: Does the page show a company filter?

questions.question: What language do you want the job postings to be in?

questions.check: Does the page show a job-language filter?

questions.check: What result count did the page show before the filter, and what count after?
questions.say_example: I filtered, and the list got bigger - <5> to <6>. The site's filters aren't working right. I'll check each result myself instead of trusting them.

questions.check: What remote and onsite filter options does the page show?
questions.say_example: Filtered to <remote>, per your ask.

questions.question: Do you want to filter the job listings by a specific country or territory?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent decide means it might skip geographic filters and apply to roles in countries where you do not live or lack work authorization.
questions.check: What country filter does the page show?
questions.say_example: Limited results to <the United States>.

questions.question: Should you filter the search results to only show jobs with the Easy Apply option?

questions.check: Does the page show an Easy Apply filter?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might blindly trust the flawed filter options and miss out on hundreds of unlisted job opportunities.
questions.check: What total result count does the page show, and what counts do the filter categories show?
questions.say_example: The site says <500> jobs, but its own filters only account for <50>. Its filtering is unreliable, so I'm double-checking results by eye.

questions.question: Do you want to filter the search results by a specific job title from the dropdown?
questions.why: The dropdown displays specific roles like Occupational Therapist and RN with tens of thousands of listings, which can help narrow down a broad job search.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to see the distribution of available jobs across different titles and pivot your search based on market demand.
questions.check: What job-title options does the dropdown list?
questions.say_example: Narrowed to <the title you asked for>.

questions.question: Do you want to review the newly posted jobs at the top of the sorted list?
questions.why: Sorting by date revealed a new "Senior GL Accountant" role posted "Today", which might be highly relevant to apply for early.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally evaluate whether these freshly posted roles are a better fit for your career goals than the default results.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the agency to abandon the application if the required effort suddenly exceeds their threshold.
questions.check: Did clicking apply open an external portal, and does it require an account?
questions.say_example: The apply button went to <an external portal> that needed its own account. I set one up and continued there.

questions.question: Did clicking the external 'Apply' button lead to the specific active job requisition, or did it redirect to a 404 error or generic corporate homepage?
questions.why: Job boards often cache postings for days or weeks after the employer has closed the requisition and disabled the direct application link on their own ATS.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to recognize that the position is dead, letting the agent waste time applying to a generic talent pool or getting stuck in a broken redirect loop.
questions.check: Did the apply link open the specific job page, or an error or generic page?
questions.say_example: The apply link is dead - it goes to <a 404>. The job may already be closed. I can check <the company>'s own careers page.

questions.question: Do you want to activate a job alert with this email address and accept the associated terms?
questions.why: Clicking activate subscribes the listed email to future job notifications and constitutes agreement to the platform's terms.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the choice of whether to receive ongoing job alert emails and the opportunity to review the terms of service.
questions.check: Does the page offer a job-alert subscription, and what terms does activating agree to?
questions.say_example: Skipped the job-alert signup - you didn't ask for emails.

children.label: Sign in or register
children.note: 3.1, then 3.2 to 3.4 as the platform demands; 3.5 on a rejection; 3.6 where a code or SMS gate exists - it is the first thing nI4K meets and it ends that session. 3.7 after account creation on ERA, where the new account lands on an empty dashboard and the vacancy has to be re-found. 3.8 is account upkeep, demoed after the task in both ERA keepers.

questions.question: Should you search for jobs or log in as a returning candidate?
questions.why: The Hiring Center home screen presents distinct paths to either search for new jobs or log in to an existing profile.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to leverage their existing profile and saved application history if the agent bypasses the returning candidate login.
questions.check: Does the home screen offer both a job search and a returning-candidate login?
questions.say_example: Took the <returning candidate> path since you have an account here.

questions.question: Should you allow Amazon.jobs to access your Amazon profile information?
questions.why: This matters because the consent screen explicitly asks to share your personal name and email address with the job portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to decide whether to link your personal Amazon account to your job application.
questions.check: What data does the consent screen say will be shared with the job site?
questions.say_example: Signing in with <Amazon> shared your <name and email> with the portal - that's all it listed.

questions.question: Do you need to manually enter your first and last name since the Amazon login didn't auto-fill them?
questions.why: Although the Amazon login consent screen explicitly listed the name Bradley Harrison, the first and last name fields on the subsequent application form remained blank.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks submitting an incomplete application if the agent assumes the third-party login automatically populated their personal details.
questions.check: Are the first and last name fields filled after sign-in?
questions.say_example: The login didn't carry your name over, so I typed it in.

questions.question: Did you create the account and note the login email?
questions.why: The screen confirms the account was created and explicitly displays the email address you will need to log in from now on.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally record the specific email address and account details used for this employer's portal.
questions.check: Does the page confirm the account was created, and what login email does it show?
questions.say_example: Account created. You log in with <email> from now on. It's in the report.

questions.question: Should an account be created on this portal, and with which login?
questions.why: The portal requires an email address to create an account for applying and tracking your status.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over which of your email addresses is registered with the employer for tracking and communication.
questions.check: Does the page require an account to apply, and which sign-up methods does it offer?
questions.say_example: This site needs an account before you can apply. I'll make one with your email <e> and a password I'll save for you. OK? Or say use <Google> instead.

questions.question: Did the system advance to the dashboard even though you left the mandatory email and password fields blank?
questions.why: The screen showed the application dashboard loading immediately after clicking 'Create account', despite the required credential fields remaining visibly empty.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to log back in and track their application status because the account was created without their actual credentials.
questions.check: Did the page advance while required fields were still empty?
questions.say_example: The site moved on even though <email and password> were still blank. I don't trust what it saved. Checking the account before we go further.

questions.question: What length and character rules does the site put on the password?
questions.why: The screen explicitly states the password must be 8-11 characters long, which is an unusually restrictive maximum length that standard password generators might violate.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure the agent generates a password that actually fits within this unusually strict length limit, preventing a validation error.
questions.check: What password length and character rules does the page state?
questions.say_example: This site caps passwords at <11> characters - odd, but the one I made fits.

questions.question: What personal details and security questions do you want to use to create your applicant account?
questions.why: The portal states that your applicant profile cannot be saved until all required personal information and security questions are completed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose memorable security questions and answers, potentially making it difficult to recover your account in the future.
questions.check: Does the form require security questions, and which questions does it list?
questions.say_example: It wants answers to security questions - <your birthplace>, <your first school>. These are your account's back door. Give me answers, or I can invent random ones and keep them in the report.

questions.question: The portal rejected the password against its own rule - does the user set the new one themselves rather than the agent inventing it?
questions.why: The screen displayed a validation error stating that your password must be at least 12 characters and include specific character types before you can proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent will choose your password and security question answers, which could prevent you from accessing this employer's portal in the future.
questions.check: What password rules does the error message state?
questions.say_example: The first password was rejected - <needs 12 characters>. Made a new one that fits.

questions.question: How does the verification code or link reach you?
questions.why: The red alert banner explicitly states that account verification is required before signing in, meaning you must access your email to continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the privacy of their personal email inbox if the agent must navigate there to retrieve the verification link.
questions.check: Does the page state that a verification code or link was sent, and to which address or number?
questions.say_example: They sent a <link> to <your email>. Only you can open it. Tell me when you've clicked it and I'll carry on.

questions.question: Does the applications dashboard list any applications of your own?
questions.why: The screen shows there are no applications to view, requiring a choice on how to return to the job search to find a posting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to verify whether your expected application history is genuinely empty before starting a new search.
questions.check: Does the dashboard show any applications?
questions.say_example: The new account's dashboard is empty, as expected. Went back to the job page.

questions.question: Does the user enter their own email and password to reach the new account, rather than handing those credentials to the agent?
questions.why: The screen displays a login form with options to enter an email and password, create an account, or search for jobs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to securely handle their own login credentials and verify they are accessing the correct account.
questions.check: What sign-in fields does the page show?
questions.say_example: Signed back in with your saved login.

questions.question: Starting 'Forgot Password?' sends a reset into the user's personal inbox and replaces their password - does the user take that over?
questions.why: The login page includes a 'Forgot Password?' link to help you establish a new password using your secret questions and personal email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose direct control over your account security and might be unaware if the agent triggers a password reset email to your personal inbox.
questions.check: Does the login page show a password-reset link?
questions.say_example: Started the password reset from the <Forgot Password> link.

questions.question: Which email address is associated with your account?
questions.why: The screen requires the email address linked to the account in order to initiate a password reset and continue the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might enter the wrong email address, sending the password reset link to an incorrect or inaccessible inbox.
questions.check: What email does the reset form ask for?
questions.say_example: Used <your email> for the reset.

questions.question: What are the exact answers to your secret security questions?
questions.why: The portal requires case-sensitive answers to specific secret questions like your birthplace and mother's maiden name to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the privacy of highly sensitive personal security answers that could be used to compromise other accounts.
questions.check: Which secret questions does the recovery form show, and does it state answers are case-sensitive?
questions.say_example: Recovery asks for <your mother's maiden name> and <your birthplace>, exactly as you first typed them. Those secrets are yours - type them yourself, or tell me and I'll fill them.

children.label: Build the marketplace profile
children.note: 4.1 before the account exists, then 4.2 to 4.8 in the order the platform's own nags suggest. only 8dGC walks this goal - and the application in 6 reads from what it builds, which is where the changes to the profile show up.

questions.question: Should you complete the remaining profile steps, such as adding a resume and headline, before searching for jobs?
questions.why: The screen displays a profile completion checklist indicating that finishing these remaining items will unlock better job matches and help you stand out.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to invest time in fully completing their platform profile to attract employers or to skip ahead to browsing job postings.
questions.check: What completion steps does the profile checklist show?
questions.say_example: Finished only the profile steps the application actually required.

questions.question: What name should you enter for your application profile?
questions.why: The application form requires a name to identify your profile and associate it with your submitted materials.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to use your full legal name, a preferred name, or a professional alias for this specific employer.
questions.check: What name field does the profile form show?
questions.say_example: Profile name set to <your name> from your resume.

questions.question: Should I upload a profile picture right now?
questions.why: The screen advises that adding an attractive profile picture increases the chance of being seen by employers.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the potential advantage of increased visibility and appeal to employers that a profile picture might provide.
questions.check: Does the profile ask for a photo, and does the page say a photo affects visibility?
questions.say_example: It wants a profile photo and says one helps you get seen. I don't have one in your files. Add one, or skip?

questions.question: Does the page's own completion indicator agree that the profile is done?
questions.why: The audio claims the profile is finished, but the visual evidence shows a 30% completion banner and a tooltip asking for more videos.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to submit a strong, fully completed application if the agent ignores the visual warnings and stops early.
questions.check: What completion percentage or missing items does the profile banner show?
questions.say_example: The profile isn't done - the banner says <30%> and it still wants <more videos>. I won't call it finished until that clears.

questions.question: Should you upload a resume and add references, or just review the existing profile sections?
questions.why: The screen shows an 'Add Resume' button and a 'Request References' option, indicating that additional supporting documents and contacts can be included.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to strengthen their application with a formatted resume document and professional references.
questions.check: Does the profile show options to add a resume and references?
questions.say_example: Added your resume to the profile. Left references for when an employer asks.

questions.question: Which account type should you pick to apply?
questions.why: The screen requires you to choose between 'I want to hire' and 'I want a job', which dictates the features and permissions your new account will have.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty that the agent will correctly register them as a job seeker rather than an employer.
questions.check: Which account types does the page offer?
questions.say_example: Picked <I want a job> - you're here to work, not hire.

questions.question: What does the profile form ask for that your materials don't supply?
questions.why: The application form prompts for a YouTube link, a description of your work, your specific roles like Scriptwriter, and how you connected with the client.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the opportunity to handpick the specific project that best highlights your skills and accurately describe your exact contributions to the employer.
questions.check: Which portfolio fields does the form show, and which are required?
questions.say_example: The profile wants <links to your six best videos> and <what you did on each>. That's your work to name - tell me and I'll fill it in.

questions.question: Should you continue without adding the six videos despite the warning that you might miss out on employers?
questions.why: The system displayed a warning modal explicitly stating that failing to add six successful videos reduces the chance of being selected by most employers.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to weigh the time cost of recording additional videos against the risk of submitting a less competitive job application.
questions.check: What does the warning say happens if the videos are not added?
questions.say_example: It warns that skipping the <six videos> means most employers won't pick you. Skip anyway, or add them first?

questions.question: How should you describe your current or last job?
questions.why: The application form requires specific details about your most recent role, including the title, description, relevant links, and exact start and end dates.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to carefully frame your most recent work experience and highlight the specific projects or links that best showcase your skills.
questions.check: What fields does the job-history form show?
questions.say_example: Filled your last job from the resume - <title>, <dates>, <description>.

questions.question: Which job types and work locations should I indicate you are available for?
questions.why: The screen presents a modal asking for your preferred job types, such as full-time or part-time, and locations, like remote or onsite.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to restrict your profile to the specific work arrangements and geographic locations you actually want.
questions.check: Which job types and locations does the availability form list?
questions.say_example: The profile asks what work you'll take - <full or part time>, <remote or onsite>. That's yours to set. What do you want shown?

questions.question: Should your salary expectations be visible on your public profile?
questions.why: This matters because the screen presents a toggle that dictates whether your financial expectations are shared publicly or kept private.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to control your privacy regarding financial expectations, which could impact your leverage in future salary negotiations.
questions.check: Does the page show a toggle for public salary visibility?
questions.say_example: Kept your pay expectations off your public profile.

questions.question: What are your salary expectations for hourly, full-time, and project-based work?
questions.why: The screen prompts for specific monetary rates across different employment types, which establishes your baseline compensation requirements for the employer.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to strategically calibrate your asking price based on your personal financial goals and the specific role.
questions.check: Which pay fields does the form show - hourly, salary, or per-project?
questions.say_example: It asks your rates: <hourly>, <full-time>, and <per project>. Employers filter on these. What numbers do you want?

questions.question: Which portfolio links do you want to include in your application?
questions.why: The application provides optional fields to link a YouTube channel, Twitter, Behance, or a personal website to demonstrate your skills.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to curate exactly which personal projects and social media profiles are shared with the employer.
questions.check: Which optional link fields does the form show?
questions.say_example: Added your <website and LinkedIn> from your materials. Left the rest blank.

questions.question: Should you add or edit the listed skills to better match this specific job?
questions.why: The screen displays existing skills like 'Computer Repair' and 'Fast Learner' with options to add or edit them, allowing you to tailor your profile for the role.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to strategically select and highlight nuanced personal strengths or recent skills that an automated agent might not know to include.
questions.check: Which skills does the profile list, and which does the job posting name?
questions.say_example: Kept your skills list to what your resume backs up.

questions.question: Does the profile now show the role the 'Select Your Main Role' modal was meant to save?
questions.why: The 'Select Your Main Role' modal failed to save and close after clicking the button, likely because multiple roles were selected when only one is permitted, forcing you to abandon the changes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might get stuck in an infinite loop trying to save invalid selections or abandon the profile setup entirely without realizing why it failed.
questions.check: Did the modal close, and does the profile now show the saved selection?
questions.say_example: The save quietly failed - the role I picked isn't on the profile. Retrying with <one role> selected.

questions.question: Which languages are you proficient in?
questions.why: The application includes a language skills section that asks you to select your proficient languages from a list.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to accurately report all the languages they speak, potentially missing a competitive advantage for the role.
questions.check: Which languages does the form ask about?
questions.say_example: Listed <the languages on your resume>.

questions.question: Do you want to receive instant notifications, and will you update your browser settings to allow them?
questions.why: The screen explicitly warned that current browser settings prevent notifications, meaning toggling them on without clicking 'Allow Notifications' is ineffective.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to properly configure their browser to receive real-time job alerts on their device.
questions.check: Does the page warn that browser settings block notifications?
questions.say_example: Left site notifications off.

questions.question: Does the About section actually contain the drafted summary before moving on?
questions.why: The screen showed an AI-generated summary being created for the profile, but it was never pasted and saved into the actual About section.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to ensure their professional summary sounds authentic and accurately reflects their personal brand.
questions.check: Does the About section now contain the drafted text?
questions.say_example: The About text I drafted never landed in the profile - the box is still empty. Pasting it again and checking it sticks.

questions.question: Should I copy the link to request reviews from your past clients?
questions.why: The screen displays an 'Ask for Review' modal with a shareable link intended to gather client feedback and strengthen the profile.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether and when to solicit reviews from their professional network to boost their profile's credibility.
questions.check: Does the page offer a shareable review-request link?
questions.say_example: There's a link to ask your past clients for reviews. I won't send anything to anyone. Want the link in the report?

children.label: Complete the application form
children.note: 5.1 and 5.2 at the door. 5.3 only where the Apply click dumped the chosen job (15nS, dz2Z). then 5.4 to 5.12 in the wizard's fixed order, each section committed with its own Save and Continue - no keeper navigates back across sections. 5.13 when a commit bounces. 5.14 wherever a progress bar or checklist shows the road ahead.

questions.question: Should you discard this application or continue?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Discard application?' confirmation dialog after closing the application modal, requiring a choice to either discard or save your progress.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the discretion to manually abort an application that you no longer wish to pursue.
questions.check: What does the confirmation dialog say happens to the application?
questions.say_example: The site tried to discard the half-done application - I kept it as a draft.

questions.question: Does your LinkedIn headline match the role you're applying for?
questions.why: The application modal prominently displays your current headline ("CMO | Digital Marketing & Brand Strategy Expert"), which the employer will see, and it might not align with the "Customer Service Loyalty Specialist" role you are applying to.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to update their LinkedIn headline to better match the target job before submitting the application, potentially confusing the recruiter.
questions.check: What headline does the profile preview show, and what role is the application for?
questions.say_example: The employer will see your profile headline - <CMO> - next to an application for <customer service>. They may read that as a mismatch. Want the headline changed first?

questions.question: Which references do you want to hand over, given the form requires them now?
questions.why: Many applicants prefer to protect their references' privacy until they know the employer is seriously considering them.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the discretion to withhold their network's contact details until a later, more appropriate stage in the hiring process.
questions.check: Does the form require reference names and contact details before submission?
questions.say_example: This form wants your references' names and numbers before any interview. That's their contact details going to a stranger. Who do you want to give, if anyone?

questions.question: Which method do you want to use to start the application?
questions.why: The screen presents multiple options to begin, such as autofilling with a resume or applying manually, which determines how your information will be entered.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to save time by autofilling from a resume or to control the exact data entry by applying manually.
questions.check: Which start options does the application offer?
questions.say_example: Started from your resume and checked every field it filled.

questions.question: Do you accept the data processing and privacy terms to continue?
questions.why: The screen requires you to acknowledge the job requirements and consent to your personal data being processed by third parties like Amazon and Salesforce.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to read the detailed privacy terms and make an informed decision about how your personal data will be handled and shared.
questions.check: What consents does the page require to continue?
questions.say_example: Agreed to the required <data processing> terms - the application can't be sent without them.

questions.question: Do you consent to Amazon retaining your application data for future opportunities?
questions.why: The account creation form requires a decision on whether the company can keep your personal data on file for other roles.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose direct control over your privacy preferences regarding long-term data retention by the employer.
questions.check: Does the form ask consent to keep your data for future roles, and is it optional?
questions.say_example: Said no to keeping your data on file for other roles - you can opt in later if you want.

questions.question: Does the application require you to agree to an unpaid 'test project' or trial period as a condition of submitting?
questions.why: Predatory postings sometimes use the application and screening process to extract free labor or intellectual property under the guise of an assessment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to spot and reject exploitative hiring practices before legally agreeing to give away their work for free.
questions.check: Does the application state that an unpaid test, trial, or sample project is required?
questions.say_example: This one requires <an unpaid test project> before you can even submit. That's free work for them. Still want in?

questions.why: The screen outlines a multi-step onboarding process, including identity verification and a 30-minute assessment, that must be finished to start tasking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally handle sensitive identity and tax setup steps or gauge the actual time commitment required for the project assessments.
questions.check: What onboarding steps and time estimates does the checklist show?
questions.say_example: Applying isn't the end here. Onboarding needs <an ID check> and <a 30-minute assessment> before any work starts.

questions.question: Should you click 'Answer questions' to complete the employer's required assessment, or close the confirmation dialog?
questions.why: The post-apply dialog displayed an 'Answer questions' button instead of a 'Done' button, indicating that further action is required to fully complete the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to be considered for the role if the agent simply closes the dialog and fails to complete the mandatory follow-up questions.
questions.check: Does the post-submit dialog show further required questions?
questions.say_example: It says submitted, but there's still <a question set> the employer requires. The application isn't really in until that's done.

questions.question: Do the two screens state the same time for the assessment?
questions.why: The dashboard initially estimated 20-30 minutes, but the 'Getting Started' screen contradicts this by advising you to set aside 15 minutes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating to an agent means you miss out on spotting this inconsistency, leaving you uncertain about the actual time commitment required.
questions.check: What time estimates do the two screens state?
questions.say_example: One screen says <20 to 30 minutes>, the next says <15>. Plan for the longer one.

questions.question: Are you ready to begin the proctored online assessment in a single sitting?
questions.why: The instructions require you to complete the assessment within four hours in one sitting while your video and audio are recorded.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally complete the assessment, which requires your physical presence for video and audio proctoring.
questions.check: What do the assessment rules state about recording, timing, and sittings?
questions.say_example: This assessment records your <video and audio>, is timed, and must be done in one sitting. It has to be you - I can read you each question, but the answers are yours. Ready, or later?

questions.question: The posting requires an assessment of its own - does the user sit it themselves rather than the agent answering for them?
questions.why: The screen shows that the Hourly Retail Associate Assessment is required for the Online Order Filling Team Associate position and will take 20 to 30 minutes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent completes a lengthy skills or personality assessment on your behalf, which might misrepresent your actual traits and abilities to the employer.
questions.check: Which assessment does the page require for the position?
questions.say_example: The required test is <the Retail Associate Assessment>, about <25 minutes>.

children.label: Take the assessment
children.note: 8.2.1, then 8.2.2 to 8.2.5 in the fixed order, then 8.2.6; no back navigation beyond one question in 8.2.4.

questions.question: What are the rules and instructions for this assessment section?
questions.why: The screen outlines critical constraints for the assessment, such as automatically advancing and only being able to go back one question.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might miss critical constraints like the inability to review past answers or how to interpret specific terms like 'supervisor'.
questions.check: What navigation rules does the assessment state?
questions.say_example: Rule for this section: it auto-advances, and you can only go back <one> question. Answer like there's no undo.

questions.question: How do you answer the assessment question on screen?
questions.why: This matters because you must accurately report your employment stability by selecting the correct time range from the provided options.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this to an agent means losing the opportunity to personally calculate and verify the exact time range that best represents your longest employment tenure.
questions.check: What question and answer options does the assessment page show?
questions.say_example: The next one is <the question>. The options run <from 'the very best' to 'needing development'>. Only you can answer this - what'll it be?

questions.question: How should you interpret the work history questions if this is your first job?
questions.why: The assessment instructions explicitly state that candidates without previous work experience should base their answers on their academic and extracurricular accomplishments.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the specific guidance on how to validly complete the assessment without work experience, potentially leading to abandoned or poorly answered questions.
questions.check: What do the instructions say candidates without work experience should base answers on?
questions.say_example: If you've never had a job, the rules here say answer from school and activities instead. Same honesty, different source.

children.label: Verify the identity
children.note: 8.3.1 to 8.3.3 in order; 8.3.4 loops back to 8.3.1 with a different document; then 8.3.5.

questions.question: Do you consent to Persona's terms for processing your biometric data?
questions.why: The application requires explicit consent for a third-party vendor to collect and process your biometric information to verify your identity.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to review the privacy policy and decide whether they are comfortable sharing highly sensitive biometric data.
questions.check: What does the consent screen say about collecting and processing biometric data, and by whom?
questions.say_example: Next step hands your <ID> and <face scan> to <Persona>, a third party, and you have to consent to biometric processing. That's your body as data - your call. Go ahead?

questions.question: The identity check needs a live camera selfie or QR scan the agent cannot perform - does the user take over that step?
questions.why: The application requires access to a camera to verify your identity via a QR code or secure link.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An AI agent cannot physically scan a QR code with a mobile device or take a live selfie to pass the identity check.
questions.check: Does the page require a phone camera via QR code or link?
questions.say_example: This part moves to your phone - it wants your camera and your <ID> in hand. I'll wait right here while you do it.

questions.question: How do you want to handle the identity verification failure?
questions.why: The screen showed a 'Verification Failed' popup stating your identity could not be verified, which might prevent a successful submission.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to troubleshoot the verification error or provide alternative details to ensure the application goes through.
questions.check: What does the failure message say, and what retry options does the page offer?
questions.say_example: The ID check failed. The page offers <a retry> or <a different document>. It's your ID - which do you want to try?

questions.question: What is the final status of your application?
questions.why: The screen indicates that your identity or account is under review, meaning your application is pending rather than fully processed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate awareness that your account requires a manual review before the employer can process your application.
questions.check: What status does the verification or review step show?
questions.say_example: You're submitted, but the ID check sits at <pending review>. Nothing left to do until they clear it - I'll note it in the report.

children.label: Track the application
children.note: 9.1 where a confirmation renders. 9.2 and 9.3 where a dashboard exists. 9.4 and 9.5 where offered.

questions.question: What do you want to do now that your application is submitted?
questions.why: The confirmation screen offers options to download a copy of the application, view its status in your dashboard, or return to the vacancy listing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to save a personal copy of the application for your records or immediately review your dashboard.
questions.check: What options does the confirmation screen offer?
questions.say_example: Saved a copy of the application and noted the dashboard link.

questions.question: What does the confirmation page say was submitted, and when?
questions.why: The screen displayed a 'Thank You!' message confirming the successful submission, which proves the application process is complete.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate reassurance of seeing the success message confirming their application was received by the employer.
questions.check: What does the confirmation page state about the submission?
questions.say_example: It's in. The page says <thank you, application received>, at <time>. Your copy and the details are in the report.

questions.question: Does the closing date on the submission dashboard match what was shown during the application?
questions.why: The application badge stated the vacancy closes in two days, but the post-submission dashboard stated it closes in three days.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses awareness of a platform inconsistency regarding the application deadline, which could affect their expectations for the hiring timeline.
questions.check: What closing date does the dashboard show, and what did the application page show?
questions.say_example: The deadline moved between pages - <two days> during the application, <three> on the dashboard. If you're counting on the extra day, don't.
